candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement): participate in quality-improvement processes, use evidence/references for improvement actions, and evaluate the effect of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — appropriate interpretation and use of heart-failure performance measures for quality improvement
candidate.educational_objective: Use heart-failure performance-measure data to evaluate defined care processes and guide quality improvement while respecting measure exclusions and individualized clinical judgment.

options.A: Compare eligible patients with the defined measure criteria and exclusions, then use the results to identify gaps in evidence-based care and guide quality improvement.
options.B: Treat every measure failure as proof that an individual clinician provided negligent care without reviewing patient-specific exclusions or circumstances.
options.C: Use performance measures to replace individualized clinical judgment whenever the measure and the client's treatment plan differ.
options.D: Apply performance measures only in academic hospitals because they are not intended to evaluate care processes in other health systems.

candidate.rationale: The 2024 ACC/AHA heart-failure performance-measure update describes performance measures as evidence-based metrics appropriate for reporting and quality measures as metrics useful for quality improvement, with defined exceptions and exclusions. Current heart-failure guidance also notes that performance measures focus on processes of care and that registry feedback can support improvement in quality. Therefore, the correct use is to review eligible cases against the measure definition and use aggregate findings to identify care-process gaps. B ignores exclusions and overattributes causation, C misuses a measure as a substitute for clinical judgment, and D incorrectly restricts quality measurement to academic centers.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports using defined heart-failure performance/quality measures, including exclusions, to evaluate care processes and support quality improvement rather than replacing individualized care decisions or assigning fault without case review.
candidate.source_document_title: 2024 Update to the 2020 ACC/AHA Clinical Performance and Quality Measures for Adults With Heart Failure
candidate.source_locator: ACC/AHA 2024 focused update → overview/key points: performance measures are evidence-based metrics suitable for public reporting or pay-for-performance; quality measures may be useful for quality improvement; exceptions and exclusions are specified for measures. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA HF Guideline → Section 12.1 Performance Measurement: performance measures focus on processes of care at clinician/facility/system levels and registry feedback may improve quality.
candidate.source_organization: American College of Cardiology / American Heart Association
candidate.stem: A hospital quality-improvement team reviews its heart-failure performance-measure data. Which use of these data is most appropriate?
